title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 4.1.3 Conditions for Swalah

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Before the first Allahu Akbar, certain conditions must already be true, or the swalah is not valid. In this sub-strand you will state those conditions, practise purity and modest dress, and learn how to find the Qibla and the time of each prayer.

## Strand 4.0: Devotional Acts
Sub-strand 4.1.3: Conditions for Swalah
Suggested lessons: 3

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 4.0 Devotional Acts, Sub-strand 4.1.3 Conditions for Swalah
• Sunan Abu Dawud: children are commanded to pray at seven
• Islamic practice: the five prayer times and the Qibla towards the Ka’bah; from Kenya that direction is generally northwards

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity
b) demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life
c) acknowledge the need for observing the condition for swalah for its validity

## Key inquiry questions
1. How would you identify time for swalah and direction of Qibla

PAGE 2: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• mention the conditions for swalah and write them in their notebook
• discuss the conditions for swalah and present in class
• demonstrate some of the conditions for swalah such as wudhu, appropriate dress code, individually
• demonstrate appropriate use of digital devices/direction of the sun in identifying direction of Qibla, individually/in pairs/groups
• discuss how to determine times for swalah and present in class

## Core competencies
• Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with digital technology is enhanced as learners demonstrate appropriate use of digital devices in identifying direction of Qibla.
• Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of interpretation and inference is enhanced as learners demonstrate appropriate use of digital devices/direction of the sun in identifying direction of Qibla, individually/in pairs/groups
• Self-efficacy: the skill of effective communication is enhanced as learners demonstrate some of the conditions for swalah such as wudhu, appropriate dress code, individually.

## Values
• Responsibility: accountability enhanced as learners demonstrate some of the conditions for swalah such as wudhu, appropriate dress code, individually
• Unity: cooperation is enhanced as learners work together to discuss the conditions for swalah, in pairs or groups, and present in class
• Respect: enhanced as learners respect each other’s opinion as they discuss how to determine times for swalah, in pairs /groups, and present in class

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Health issues: Personal hygiene as a requirement for swalah

## Links to other learning areas
• Social Studies: as learners learn finding directions on the compass.

PAGE 3: Lesson 1: The conditions that come before swalah

LESSON 1: THE CONDITIONS THAT COME BEFORE SWALAH
================================================

## What you will learn
• State the conditions for swalah.
• Explain the difference between a condition and an action inside the prayer.
• Give a reason why each condition is required.

Curriculum outcomes: a) state the conditions for swalah as a requirement for its validity; c) acknowledge the need for observing the condition for swalah for its validity

## Introduction
A beautiful rukuu cannot repair a prayer performed before its time, in the wrong direction, or in clothes that do not cover the awrah. Those matters are conditions. They must be in place before the prayer counts.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: The conditions that come before swalah — Notes 2

## Notes

### Conditions to write down
In this Grade 4 study, state these conditions for swalah:

1. The person is a Muslim and is of sound mind. A young child is taught to pray before the duty becomes fully obligatory at puberty. The Prophet (S.A.W.) told parents to command children to pray at seven years of age (Abu Dawud).
2. The time of that prayer has entered. Fajr is not prayed in the middle of the morning and called Fajr.
3. The person has wudhu, or ghusl if ghusl is required, and the body, clothes and place are free from najasa.
4. The awrah is covered with a decent dress.
5. The person faces the Qibla, the direction of the Ka’bah in Makkah.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: The conditions that come before swalah — Why they matter

The intention, niyyah, is studied with the pillars of swalah in the next sub-strand, because this curriculum places it among the pillars. Do not drop it from your prayer. Do list the five conditions above as the conditions.

### Why they matter
A condition is something the prayer depends on. If the time has not entered, you are early, not yet in that swalah. If the awrah is uncovered when you were able to cover it, the prayer is not valid. If you face the opposite of the Qibla on purpose, you have turned away from the Ka’bah that the Muslim world faces.

Write the five conditions in your notebook in an order you can remember: who prays, when, in what state of purity, in what dress, and towards where. Acknowledging them means you check them before you begin, every day, not only in an examination.

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: The conditions that come before swalah — Example 1

## Key words
• condition of swalah — something that must be true for the prayer to be valid
• Qibla — the direction of the Ka’bah in Makkah
• awrah — the part of the body that must be covered

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A boy has wudhu and a clean shirt, but he begins Dhuhr ten minutes before the time, facing the back wall of the mosque. Which conditions has he missed?

Working:
1. The time of Dhuhr has not entered.
2. He is not facing the Qibla if the congregation faces the opposite way.
3. Wudhu and clean clothes have been met, but they do not replace the other conditions.

Answer: He missed the correct time and the Qibla. He should wait for the time and face the Ka’bah.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: The conditions that come before swalah — Write and present the conditions

## Activity: Write and present the conditions
You will need: Notebook, Manila paper

1. Mention the five conditions aloud as a class.

2. Each group writes them on manila paper in clear words.

3. Present the list and give one example of what happens if a condition is missing.

4. Copy the corrected list into your notebook.

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: The conditions that come before swalah — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. List the five conditions for swalah taught in this lesson.

2. At what age did the Prophet (S.A.W.) say children should be commanded to pray?

3. Why is facing the Qibla called a condition?

## Answers to practice

1. Being a Muslim of sound mind, the time having entered, ritual purity and freedom from najasa, covering the awrah, and facing the Qibla.

2. At seven years of age.

3. The prayer depends on it. The worshipper faces the Ka’bah in Makkah.

## Summary
• The conditions include Islam and a sound mind, the right time, purity, covering the awrah, and facing the Qibla.
• A missing condition is not repaired by a correct rukuu.
• Children are taught to pray from the age of seven.

PAGE 9: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Purity you can demonstrate

LESSON 2: PURITY AND THE DRESS FOR SWALAH
=========================================

## What you will learn
• Demonstrate readiness in wudhu and cleanliness.
• State how a boy and a girl cover the awrah for swalah.
• Check body, clothes and place before praying.

Curriculum outcomes: b) demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life

## Introduction
Two conditions can be seen by looking carefully: whether the person is ready in purity, and whether the dress covers what must be covered. This lesson practises both.

## Notes

### Purity you can demonstrate
Before swalah, show these checks:

- You have wudhu, and you renew it if a nullifier has happened.
- Your body is free from najasa. A splash of urine on the leg is washed.
- Your clothes are free from najasa.
- The mat or the ground where you will pray is free from najasa.

These checks link twahara, wudhu and swalah. Personal hygiene supports them: a clean mouth, trimmed nails and clothes that are not soaked in mud make the prayer more fitting, even where mud itself is not najasa.

PAGE 10: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Dress

### Dress
For swalah, a boy covers the awrah from the navel to the knees. The cloth should not be so thin that the skin is seen, and it should stay in place during rukuu and sujud. A shirt that gapes open at the waist when he bows needs to be arranged before he starts.

A girl covers her whole body except the face and the hands. The cloth should be opaque, not see-through, and it should cover the hair, the arms and the legs. School uniform is checked against this rule at prayer time. If the uniform does not cover the awrah, a prayer garment is added.

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Demonstration

### Demonstration
Each learner can show, without making a joke of it, how the dress is arranged and how the place is inspected. The teacher guides boys and girls appropriately. The point is responsibility: you look at your own clothes before Allahu Akbar, instead of hoping nobody noticed.

## Key words
• opaque — thick enough that the skin cannot be seen through the cloth
• prayer garment — an extra clean covering used so that the awrah is covered in swalah

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Example 1

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A girl’s school dress has short sleeves and she has a clean scarf and a long prayer dress in her bag. What should she do before swalah?

Working:
1. The awrah of a girl in swalah is the whole body except the face and the hands.
2. Short sleeves do not meet that condition.
3. She wears the prayer dress and scarf over the uniform if needed, and she checks that she has wudhu.

Answer: She covers her awrah with the prayer dress and scarf, and she prays only when purity and dress are both in place.

## Activity: Demonstrate purity and dress
You will need: A prayer mat, A basin of water for wudhu if the school allows, A modest extra garment for demonstration

1. Individually, show the checks: wudhu, clean body, clean clothes and a clean place. Use actions the teacher has approved.

2. State the awrah for a boy and for a girl.

3. Arrange a garment so that it will not open during rukuu.

4. A partner names any condition you forgot to mention.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. What part of the body must a boy cover in swalah?

2. What must a girl cover in swalah?

3. Name the four purity checks before Allahu Akbar.

## Answers to practice

1. From the navel to the knees.

2. Her whole body except the face and the hands, in cloth that is not see-through.

3. Wudhu, a body free from najasa, clothes free from najasa, and a place free from najasa.

## Summary
• Purity of wudhu, body, clothes and place can be checked before every prayer.
• A boy covers from the navel to the knees. A girl covers all but the face and the hands.
• Dress is arranged before the prayer so that rukuu does not uncover the awrah.

PAGE 14: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla

LESSON 3: THE TIME OF SWALAH AND THE DIRECTION OF THE QIBLA
===========================================================

## What you will learn
• Describe how to know that the time of a prayer has entered.
• Find the Qibla using a mosque, a compass, a digital device or the sun’s general direction.
• Explain why both conditions are observed every day.

Curriculum outcomes: b) demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life; c) acknowledge the need for observing the condition for swalah for its validity

## Introduction
Kenya lies south of Makkah, so the Qibla from Kenya is generally northwards. The clock time of Dhuhr changes through the year. A Muslim therefore learns a method, not one frozen minute on the wall.

PAGE 15: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Knowing the time

## Notes

### Knowing the time
There are five obligatory prayers:

- Fajr: from true dawn until sunrise
- Dhuhr: after the sun has passed its highest point, through the middle of the day
- Asr: in the afternoon, before sunset
- Maghrib: just after sunset
- Isha: at night, when the twilight has gone

You can know that the time has entered by the adhan of a trusted mosque, by a timetable prepared for your area, or by a digital prayer-time tool that a teacher or parent has checked. The sun helps you understand the names: Fajr is before the sun rises, Maghrib is just after it sets, and you do not pray Dhuhr while the sun is still climbing to the middle of the sky. Do not invent a single clock time for the whole country. The time moves.

PAGE 16: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Notes 3

### Knowing the Qibla
The Qibla is the direction of the Ka’bah. From Kenya, Makkah is to the north, so the Qibla is generally northwards. The exact line is not the same in every town, so confirm it in one of these ways:

- Face the way the local mosque faces.
- Use a compass with a known Qibla bearing that a teacher has explained.
- Use a Qibla application on a digital device, standing in an open place, with an adult checking it.
- Use the sun to avoid a wrong direction: the sun rises in the east and sets in the west. The Qibla is not “towards sunrise” or “towards sunset”. It is towards Makkah, generally north from Kenya.

PAGE 17: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Notes 4

If you are travelling and truly cannot find the direction after trying, ask a Muslim who knows the place. Guessing in a city that has a mosque is not enough. Observing time and Qibla every day shows that you accept these conditions as part of a valid swalah.

## Key words
• adhan — the call to prayer that announces that the time has entered
• true dawn — the light across the horizon that begins the time of Fajr

PAGE 18: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Example 1

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner faces the sunrise for Fajr and says, “The bright sky is the Qibla.” What two corrections does he need?

Working:
1. Sunrise is in the east. From Kenya the Qibla is generally north, towards Makkah.
2. He should confirm the direction by the mosque, a compass or a checked digital tool.
3. He also checks that Fajr time is still before sunrise. Once the sun has risen, Fajr time has ended.

Answer: He should not treat east as the Qibla, and he must pray Fajr before sunrise. He confirms northwards towards Makkah by a reliable method.

PAGE 19: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Find the time and the Qibla

## Activity: Find the time and the Qibla
You will need: A compass or a digital Qibla tool used with the teacher, The school’s direction of the mosque if one is nearby, Notebook

1. Discuss how your family knows that Maghrib or Isha has entered: adhan, timetable or a checked device.

2. In pairs or groups, use the compass, the mosque direction or the digital tool to identify the Qibla at school.

3. Observe where the sun is and state which way is east, then turn to the Qibla you have confirmed.

4. Write the five prayer names and the method you used for the Qibla.

## Practice

1. When does the time of Fajr begin and end?

2. Name two reliable ways to know that a prayer time has entered.

3. From Kenya, in which general direction is the Qibla, and how do you confirm it?

4. Why must both time and Qibla be observed?

PAGE 20: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Answers to practice

## Answers to practice

1. It begins at true dawn and ends at sunrise.

2. Any two: the adhan of a trusted mosque, a timetable for your area, or a digital tool checked by a teacher or parent.

3. Generally northwards, towards Makkah. Confirm it by the mosque, a compass or a checked Qibla device, not by facing sunrise or sunset.

4. Each is a condition for the validity of swalah.

## Summary
• Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha each have a real time that you confirm, not a guessed hour.
• From Kenya the Qibla is generally northwards, towards Makkah, and it should be confirmed.
• The sun shows east and west. It is not itself the Qibla.

PAGE 21: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which set lists conditions for swalah?
   A. A football, a whistle and a score
   B. Purity, covering the awrah, the right time and facing the Qibla
   C. Only a loud voice
   D. Skipping wudhu if you are late

2. From what age are children to be commanded to pray?
   A. Three
   B. Seven
   C. Twenty
   D. Only after marriage

3. A boy’s awrah in swalah is…
   A. The face only
   B. From the navel to the knees
   C. The hair only
   D. The hands only

4. A girl in swalah covers…
   A. Only her hair
   B. The whole body except the face and the hands
   C. Only the knees
   D. Nothing extra over a short dress

5. Fajr time ends…
   A. At midnight
   B. At sunrise
   C. At Maghrib
   D. After Isha

6. Maghrib is prayed…

7. From Kenya, the Qibla is generally…
   A. Towards sunrise
   B. Towards sunset
   C. Northwards, towards Makkah
   D. Straight down

8. A reliable way to confirm the Qibla is…
   A. Facing whatever wall is nearest
   B. Using the mosque direction, a compass or a checked digital tool
   C. Following the sunrise
   D. Closing your eyes and pointing

9. Why does najasa on the prayer place matter?
   A. Purity of the place is part of the conditions
   B. Dust is always mughalladha
   C. The mat replaces wudhu
   D. Time does not matter

10. Why does a learner check time, dress, purity and Qibla before every prayer?

PAGE 22: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. B. Purity, covering the awrah, the right time and facing the Qibla
   These must be in place for the prayer to be valid. The worshipper is also Muslim and of sound mind.

2. B. Seven
   This is the teaching reported in Sunan Abu Dawud.

3. B. From the navel to the knees
   The covering must also not be see-through, and it must stay covered in rukuu.

4. B. The whole body except the face and the hands
   The cloth should be opaque.

5. B. At sunrise
   Fajr runs from true dawn until sunrise.

6. Just after sunset.
   It is not prayed in the late morning.

7. C. Northwards, towards Makkah
   Makkah is north of Kenya. The exact line is confirmed locally.

8. B. Using the mosque direction, a compass or a checked digital tool
   The sun shows east and west, but the Qibla is the direction of the Ka’bah.

9. A. Purity of the place is part of the conditions
   Body, clothes and place are checked before swalah.

10. Because they are conditions for the validity of swalah.
   Acknowledging the conditions means observing them in daily prayers.

LESSON 2: PURITY AND THE DRESS FOR SWALAH
=========================================

## What you will learn
• Demonstrate readiness in wudhu and cleanliness.
• State how a boy and a girl cover the awrah for swalah.
• Check body, clothes and place before praying.

Curriculum outcomes: b) demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life

## Introduction

## Notes

### Purity you can demonstrate
Before swalah, show these checks:

- You have wudhu, and you renew it if a nullifier has happened.
- Your body is free from najasa. A splash of urine on the leg is washed.
- Your clothes are free from najasa.
- The mat or the ground where you will pray is free from najasa.

These checks link twahara, wudhu and swalah. Personal hygiene supports them: a clean mouth, trimmed nails and clothes that are not soaked in mud make the prayer more fitting, even where mud itself is not najasa.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Dress
studyPages.body:
### Dress
For swalah, a boy covers the awrah from the navel to the knees. The cloth should not be so thin that the skin is seen, and it should stay in place during rukuu and sujud. A shirt that gapes open at the waist when he bows needs to be arranged before he starts.

A girl covers her whole body except the face and the hands. The cloth should be opaque, not see-through, and it should cover the hair, the arms and the legs. School uniform is checked against this rule at prayer time. If the uniform does not cover the awrah, a prayer garment is added.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Demonstration
studyPages.body:
### Demonstration
Each learner can show, without making a joke of it, how the dress is arranged and how the place is inspected. The teacher guides boys and girls appropriately. The point is responsibility: you look at your own clothes before Allahu Akbar, instead of hoping nobody noticed.

## Key words
• opaque — thick enough that the skin cannot be seen through the cloth
• prayer garment — an extra clean covering used so that the awrah is covered in swalah

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Example 1
studyPages.body:
## Worked examples

### Example 1
A girl’s school dress has short sleeves and she has a clean scarf and a long prayer dress in her bag. What should she do before swalah?

Working:
1. The awrah of a girl in swalah is the whole body except the face and the hands.
2. Short sleeves do not meet that condition.
3. She wears the prayer dress and scarf over the uniform if needed, and she checks that she has wudhu.

Answer: She covers her awrah with the prayer dress and scarf, and she prays only when purity and dress are both in place.

## Activity: Demonstrate purity and dress
You will need: A prayer mat, A basin of water for wudhu if the school allows, A modest extra garment for demonstration

1. Individually, show the checks: wudhu, clean body, clean clothes and a clean place. Use actions the teacher has approved.

2. State the awrah for a boy and for a girl.

3. Arrange a garment so that it will not open during rukuu.

4. A partner names any condition you forgot to mention.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Purity and the dress for swalah — Answers to practice
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. What part of the body must a boy cover in swalah?

2. What must a girl cover in swalah?

3. Name the four purity checks before Allahu Akbar.

## Answers to practice

1. From the navel to the knees.

2. Her whole body except the face and the hands, in cloth that is not see-through.

3. Wudhu, a body free from najasa, clothes free from najasa, and a place free from najasa.

## Summary
• Purity of wudhu, body, clothes and place can be checked before every prayer.
• A boy covers from the navel to the knees. A girl covers all but the face and the hands.
• Dress is arranged before the prayer so that rukuu does not uncover the awrah.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla
studyPages.body:
LESSON 3: THE TIME OF SWALAH AND THE DIRECTION OF THE QIBLA
===========================================================

## What you will learn
• Describe how to know that the time of a prayer has entered.
• Find the Qibla using a mosque, a compass, a digital device or the sun’s general direction.
• Explain why both conditions are observed every day.

Curriculum outcomes: b) demonstrate the observable conditions for swalah in day-to- day life; c) acknowledge the need for observing the condition for swalah for its validity

## Introduction
Kenya lies south of Makkah, so the Qibla from Kenya is generally northwards. The clock time of Dhuhr changes through the year. A Muslim therefore learns a method, not one frozen minute on the wall.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Knowing the time
studyPages.body:
## Notes

### Knowing the time
There are five obligatory prayers:

- Fajr: from true dawn until sunrise
- Dhuhr: after the sun has passed its highest point, through the middle of the day
- Asr: in the afternoon, before sunset
- Maghrib: just after sunset
- Isha: at night, when the twilight has gone

You can know that the time has entered by the adhan of a trusted mosque, by a timetable prepared for your area, or by a digital prayer-time tool that a teacher or parent has checked. The sun helps you understand the names: Fajr is before the sun rises, Maghrib is just after it sets, and you do not pray Dhuhr while the sun is still climbing to the middle of the sky. Do not invent a single clock time for the whole country. The time moves.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Notes 3
studyPages.body:
### Knowing the Qibla
The Qibla is the direction of the Ka’bah. From Kenya, Makkah is to the north, so the Qibla is generally northwards. The exact line is not the same in every town, so confirm it in one of these ways:

- Face the way the local mosque faces.
- Use a compass with a known Qibla bearing that a teacher has explained.
- Use a Qibla application on a digital device, standing in an open place, with an adult checking it.
- Use the sun to avoid a wrong direction: the sun rises in the east and sets in the west. The Qibla is not “towards sunrise” or “towards sunset”. It is towards Makkah, generally north from Kenya.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Notes 4
studyPages.body:
If you are travelling and truly cannot find the direction after trying, ask a Muslim who knows the place. Guessing in a city that has a mosque is not enough. Observing time and Qibla every day shows that you accept these conditions as part of a valid swalah.

## Key words
• adhan — the call to prayer that announces that the time has entered
• true dawn — the light across the horizon that begins the time of Fajr

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Example 1
studyPages.body:
## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner faces the sunrise for Fajr and says, “The bright sky is the Qibla.” What two corrections does he need?

Working:
1. Sunrise is in the east. From Kenya the Qibla is generally north, towards Makkah.
2. He should confirm the direction by the mosque, a compass or a checked digital tool.
3. He also checks that Fajr time is still before sunrise. Once the sun has risen, Fajr time has ended.

Answer: He should not treat east as the Qibla, and he must pray Fajr before sunrise. He confirms northwards towards Makkah by a reliable method.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Find the time and the Qibla
studyPages.body:
## Activity: Find the time and the Qibla
You will need: A compass or a digital Qibla tool used with the teacher, The school’s direction of the mosque if one is nearby, Notebook

1. Discuss how your family knows that Maghrib or Isha has entered: adhan, timetable or a checked device.

2. In pairs or groups, use the compass, the mosque direction or the digital tool to identify the Qibla at school.

3. Observe where the sun is and state which way is east, then turn to the Qibla you have confirmed.

4. Write the five prayer names and the method you used for the Qibla.

## Practice

1. When does the time of Fajr begin and end?

2. Name two reliable ways to know that a prayer time has entered.

3. From Kenya, in which general direction is the Qibla, and how do you confirm it?

4. Why must both time and Qibla be observed?

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: The time of swalah and the direction of the Qibla — Answers to practice
studyPages.body:
## Answers to practice

1. It begins at true dawn and ends at sunrise.

2. Any two: the adhan of a trusted mosque, a timetable for your area, or a digital tool checked by a teacher or parent.

3. Generally northwards, towards Makkah. Confirm it by the mosque, a compass or a checked Qibla device, not by facing sunrise or sunset.

4. Each is a condition for the validity of swalah.

## Summary
• Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha each have a real time that you confirm, not a guessed hour.
• From Kenya the Qibla is generally northwards, towards Makkah, and it should be confirmed.
• The sun shows east and west. It is not itself the Qibla.

studyPages.title: Revision quiz
studyPages.body:
REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which set lists conditions for swalah?
   A. A football, a whistle and a score
   B. Purity, covering the awrah, the right time and facing the Qibla
   C. Only a loud voice
   D. Skipping wudhu if you are late

2. From what age are children to be commanded to pray?
   A. Three
   B. Seven
   C. Twenty
   D. Only after marriage

3. A boy’s awrah in swalah is…
   A. The face only
   B. From the navel to the knees
   C. The hair only
   D. The hands only

4. A girl in swalah covers…
   A. Only her hair
   B. The whole body except the face and the hands
   C. Only the knees
   D. Nothing extra over a short dress

5. Fajr time ends…
   A. At midnight
   B. At sunrise
   C. At Maghrib
   D. After Isha

6. Maghrib is prayed…

7. From Kenya, the Qibla is generally…
   A. Towards sunrise
   B. Towards sunset
   C. Northwards, towards Makkah
   D. Straight down

8. A reliable way to confirm the Qibla is…
   A. Facing whatever wall is nearest
   B. Using the mosque direction, a compass or a checked digital tool
   C. Following the sunrise
   D. Closing your eyes and pointing

9. Why does najasa on the prayer place matter?
   A. Purity of the place is part of the conditions
   B. Dust is always mughalladha
   C. The mat replaces wudhu
   D. Time does not matter

10. Why does a learner check time, dress, purity and Qibla before every prayer?

studyPages.title: Quiz answers
studyPages.body:
ANSWERS
=======

1. B. Purity, covering the awrah, the right time and facing the Qibla
   These must be in place for the prayer to be valid. The worshipper is also Muslim and of sound mind.

2. B. Seven
   This is the teaching reported in Sunan Abu Dawud.

3. B. From the navel to the knees
   The covering must also not be see-through, and it must stay covered in rukuu.

4. B. The whole body except the face and the hands
   The cloth should be opaque.

5. B. At sunrise
   Fajr runs from true dawn until sunrise.

6. Just after sunset.
   It is not prayed in the late morning.

7. C. Northwards, towards Makkah
   Makkah is north of Kenya. The exact line is confirmed locally.

8. B. Using the mosque direction, a compass or a checked digital tool
   The sun shows east and west, but the Qibla is the direction of the Ka’bah.

9. A. Purity of the place is part of the conditions
   Body, clothes and place are checked before swalah.

10. Because they are conditions for the validity of swalah.
   Acknowledging the conditions means observing them in daily prayers.
